sections.heading:
The Sum of
All Human Knowledge
sections.body: Seven million articles. Two hundred seventy-five thousand active editors. A living, breathing repository of everything humanity knows — freely available to everyone, forever.

stats.desc: Articles in English — each one a doorway to understanding
Active editors shaping knowledge every day

sections.heading: The Oregon State Capitol
sections.body: Housing the legislature of the U.S. state of Oregon and the offices of the governor and other officials. Built from 1936 to 1938, its art deco design features a 50-foot rotunda with a marble floor inlaid with 37 types of Oregon stone.

sections.heading: Curiosity Never Stops
sections.body: Every day, Wikipedia uncovers the strange, the beautiful, and the unexpected — from art heists hidden on pig farms to Picasso drawings in forgotten collections.

cards.title: 1972 Worcester Heist
cards.desc: Four paintings stolen from the Worcester Art Museum were discovered hidden on a pig farm.

cards.title: Picasso Fountain
cards.desc: "Mother and Child by a Fountain" — one of the stolen works, by Pablo Picasso himself.

cards.title: Pope Leo XIV
cards.desc: First encyclical "Magnifica Humanitas" expresses concerns about artificial intelligence.

cards.title: Cyprus Elections
cards.desc: Democratic Rally, led by Annita Demetriou, wins the most seats in parliament.

sections.heading: History Unfolds
sections.body: From Napoleonic wars to space exploration — every date on the calendar carries the weight of what came before.

cards.desc: Napoleonic Wars: A Franco-Spanish fleet recaptured ...
Festa della Repubblica — Italy became a republic.
Telangana formed as the 29th state of India.

cards.title: International
cards.desc: International Whores' Day — recognizing sex worker rights.

sections.heading: The Black Kite
sections.body: A medium-sized bird of prey found across Europe, Asia, Africa, and Australia. Like Wikipedia itself — far-reaching, adaptable, and soaring above borders.

stats.desc: Wikipedia's sister projects — Wiktionary, Commons, Wikisource, Wikiquote, and more — extend knowledge beyond the encyclopedia.
Anyone can edit. Every article is a living document shaped by the global community.
